key_insight: Learned flow-field initialization accelerates steady RANS convergence by approximately 2–4× in iterations on unseen nominal cases while retaining CFD solver correction.
engineering_relevance: Warm starts can reduce repeated aerodynamic analysis costs, with estimated campaign speed-ups of 2.1–2.3× including data generation and training.
method: A condition-modulated Transolver predicts mean-flow and turbulence fields directly on native CFD meshes.
Training combines Fourier and wall features, target-gated regularization, Sobolev-type loss and adaptive loss weighting without solver-residual evaluation.
Predicted fields initialize RANS solves; coarse-mesh models deploy on finer meshes without retraining or solution interpolation.
evidence_signal: Million-cell 3D evaluations on SuperWing, NASA CRM and DLR-F6 covered geometric and operating-condition generalization with Spalart–Allmaras and k–ω SST closures; no warm run diverged, and fewer than 2% missed the cold-reference convergence criterion.
watch_item: Initialization remains sensitive near flow separation, and iteration reductions do not directly equal end-to-end runtime savings.
paper_title: Learned Warm Starts for Steady Transonic RANS Simulations of Wing and Aircraft Configurations
